$comment: Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md. The three configuration-typed rules here check that a scale or role set is declared and referenced — not that the resulting design is good. Standard 10 R5 is explicit that this must not become pixel policing, which is why severity is warning and level is recommended.

rules.title: A typography scale is defined and used
rules.description: Type sizes come from a defined scale rather than being chosen per view.
rules.rationale: Ad-hoc sizes read as noise rather than hierarchy, and they make a global change to reading comfort impossible to perform.
rules.remediation: Define a scale and reference its steps instead of literal sizes.
rules.$assuranceNote: The declared scale source is read. Whether every size in the product comes from it is the subject of design-system.tokens-used, and is only partially observable.

rules.title: Color is defined by role rather than by value
rules.description: Colors are named for what they mean — surface, danger, on-surface — rather than for what they look like.
rules.rationale: A palette named by appearance cannot be re-themed: 'blue-500' is wrong in a dark theme in a way 'accent' is not, and every consumer has to be revisited to find out which.
rules.remediation: Name colors by role and map roles to values per theme.
rules.$assuranceNote: Role naming is visible in the token source. Whether the roles are the right ones is a design judgment.

rules.title: A shipped dark mode is designed rather than inverted
rules.description: Dark mode is optional. Where a project ships one, it is designed — contrast, elevation, and state colors are decided for it rather than produced by inverting the light theme.
rules.rationale: Inversion produces contrast failures and unreadable state colors precisely where the light theme was most carefully tuned. Shipping it is worse than shipping no dark mode.
rules.remediation: Define the dark theme's role mappings deliberately and check contrast within it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Applicable only where the project declares dark-mode support. Whether a theme was designed or derived is a judgment about the result, not a property of the files.

rules.title: A spacing scale is defined and used
rules.description: Spacing comes from a defined scale rather than from values chosen per component.
rules.rationale: Spacing is how grouping is communicated. Inconsistent spacing makes unrelated things look related, which is a meaning error rather than an aesthetic one.
rules.remediation: Define a spacing scale and reference its steps.
rules.$assuranceNote: The declared scale is read; conformance of every value to it is not asserted. Standard 10 R5 forbids turning this into pixel policing.

rules.title: Visual hierarchy reflects intended priority
rules.description: What is most important in a view is what is most prominent, and secondary material is subordinated or disclosed progressively rather than competing.
rules.rationale: A view where everything is emphasized has no hierarchy, and the user does the sorting the design declined to do.
rules.remediation: Decide the view's priority order and let prominence follow it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Priority is intent and prominence is perception. Neither is present in source; a human establishes this for the views they reviewed.

rules.title: The primary action of a view is identifiable
rules.description: Where a view has an intended next action, it is distinguishable from the alternatives without reading every one of them.
rules.rationale: A view with several equally weighted actions asks the user to reconstruct the intended path, on every visit.
rules.remediation: Give the primary action visual precedence and subordinate the rest.
rules.$assuranceNote: Which action is primary is a product decision that no scan can read from the interface.

rules.title: Visual change is evidenced rather than asserted
rules.description: A change to the interface is supported by captured evidence of what changed, rather than by a claim that nothing else did.
rules.rationale: Unintended visual change is invisible to the person who caused it. Evidence is what makes the difference between knowing and believing.
rules.remediation: Capture the affected views and record the comparison, or attest to the review with the screenshots it was performed against.
rules.$assuranceNote: A screenshot establishes what rendered, never whether it is right. Attestable because a human reviewing committed captures is a real evidence path; not-evaluated in v1.0.0 until a producer exists.
